jobs.title: Director of Cloud Architecture & Platform Engineering
jobs.description: Position Summary: We are seeking a Director of Cloud Architecture & Platform Engineering who thrives at the intersection of high-level strategy and deep-dive technical execution. This is a combined role designed for a leader who isn't afraid to open a PR or troubleshoot a production K8s cluster while simultaneously building an infrastructure roadmap. In this role, you will lead a lean, high-output team of engineers. You will spend roughly 50% of your time "on the tools"—architecting core systems and building foundational code—and the remaining time driving the team, setting strategy, and ensuring our platform meets the rigorous security demands of the healthcare industry. Responsibilities: (Technical Execution) Lead Architect: Act as the primary architect for our cloud environment, personally designing the systems that handle high-volume clinical data and PHI. Core Infrastructure Development: Building out CI/CD templates, refining our Kubernetes service mesh, migrating legacy cloud platform to a future PaaS (Platform as a Service) model Prototyping & R&D: Rapidly prototype new platform features—such as automated compliance monitoring or developer self-service portals—before handing them off to the team for scaling. Tier 3 Escalation: Act as a hands-on escalation point for complex architectural issues or critical production incidents, providing "in-the-trenches" technical leadership. Sustain environments: Sustain cloud and platform environments commensurate with “clean” environment, free of vulnerabilities, legacy code, and legacy architecture practices. (Leadership & Strategy) Team Growth: Manage and mentor a specialized team of cloud and platform engineers. Conduct code reviews not just for quality, but as teaching moments to elevate the team’s skill sets. Strategic Roadmap: Define the "Platform-as-a-Product" vision, ensuring every technical initiative directly accelerates our product's time-to-value for healthcare partners. Regulatory Governance: Partner with the Security and Compliance teams to automate HIPAA and HITRUST requirements, turning "check-box compliance" into "automated guardrails." FinOps & Budgeting: Oversee the cloud budget with a surgical eye, implementing automated cost-saving measures without sacrificing performance or reliability. Perform other duties as assigned Requirements: Experience: 5-8+ years in Cloud/Infrastructure Engineering, with at least 3-5 years in a leadership role (Lead, Manager, or Director) within a scale-up environment. Healthcare Proficiency: Deep, hands-on experience managing infrastructure within HIPAA, HITRUST, or SOC2 environments. You understand that in HealthTech, "done" means "secure and compliant." Scaling Mindset: Experience taking a platform from "early-stage scrappy" to "enterprise-grade robust" with scaling capability. Service Mindset: Operate as a direct partner to application engineering and data engineering teams, serving as an expert with cloud capabilities Skills: Advanced Stack: Expert-level proficiency in Kubernetes (EKS/AKS) and Infrastructure as Code for automation. CI/CD Pipeline Development: Mastery of automation tools to create seamless deployment workflows. Advanced knowledge of architecting secure network topologies. IAM & Governance: Deep understanding of IAM and Service Control Policies (SCPs) to enforce the principle of least privilege across a multi-account organization. Cloud FinOps & Observability: Skill in using cloud financial management tooling to balance high performance with budget management. Limited Travel, scheduled per needs of the business Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: VP Finance and HR
jobs.description: Salvo Health is a new approach to caring for the more than 100 million Americans living with chronic gut and metabolic conditions - from IBS and IBD to metabolic liver disease and obesity. Backed by leading venture capital investors with over $28 million raised, Salvo pairs patients with a whole-patient care team that includes registered dietitians, nurses, and GI-trained therapists, all guided by a technology stack built around evidence-based, personalized protocols. Unlike episodic care, Salvo delivers continuous, app-based support seven days a week—using RPM and insurance-covered codes - in partnership with each patient’s existing local physician. We extend and enhance community GI care rather than displacing it. Our investors include operators and builders from Livongo, Ro, Ginger, Brightline, Tia, and other leading health innovators. Salvo Health is transforming how patients access and experience GI care. We partner with leading GI MSOs and health systems to deliver data-driven, patient-centered solutions that improve outcomes and reduce costs. About The Role: Salvo Health is searching for a VP Finance to elevate and lead our financial operations as we work toward scaling growth following our Series A raise. This is a fully remote role, that can be based anywhere within the United States, reporting to the Chief Operating Officer. You'll own financial reporting, forecasting, and variance analysis; manage and mentor our current Finance and HR Manager; and act as a strategic and analytical partner to our CEO on fundraising and partner-facing financial matters. First 90-Day Deliverables: Rapidly assess current financial controls, refine the existing 18-month cash-flow forecast, and establish a streamlined variance analysis reporting cadence for the executive team. This role is a strong fit for an experienced finance leader who wants real ownership and strategic scope. What You Will Do: Strategic Forecasting & Modeling: Own and refine the company's financial projection models (revenue, headcount, cash-flow), driving the strategic roadmap toward cash-flow break-even post-Series A. Team Leadership & Delegation: Manage and mentor our existing Finance & HR Manager and Recruiter, ensuring smooth day-to-day operations (bookkeeping, AP/AR, payroll, and month-end close) so your hours remain focused on high-impact initiatives. Fundraising & Board Strategy: Act as the financial co-pilot to the CEO and COO for venture fundraising, driving data room preparation, cap table scenario modeling, and presenting high-level performance metrics directly to the board. Healthcare Commercial Analysis: Develop payer- and partner-facing financial models—specifically analyzing unit economics and contract structures for our specialty virtual care services—to support critical commercial and partnership discussions. Cash & Resource Strategy: Advise leadership on a strategic approach to cash management, banking relationships, and optimal budget allocation across clinical and operational departments. Financial Reporting & Controls: Oversee the delivery of accurate monthly and quarterly financial reporting, while maintaining internal controls appropriate for a scaling, venture-backed organization like variance and scenario analyses. Compensation & Benefits Strategy: Oversee the financial architecture of HR operations, including compensation banding, annual benefits renewal negotiations, and payroll compliance. Headcount Planning & HR Budgeting: Partner with the Finance & HR Manager to model headcount costs, track employee acquisition spend, and ensure the HR technology stack aligns with Salvo Health 's operational budget. Determine staffing projections and work with Recruiter to ensure adequate staffing. Payroll & Compliance Oversight: Serve as the final executive escalation point for payroll execution, state-level employment tax compliance, and benefit program funding for a remote workforce. jobs.title: Oncology Nurse Navigator
jobs.description: CancerNavigator is an early-stage healthcare company (remote, headquartered in Washington, D.C.) dedicated to supporting cancer patients in their hour of need. Our Mission & Our Work, in Brief Cancer is the number one cause of death for commercially insured Americans and the top cost driver for health plans. And, cancer patients are struggling. CancerNavigator is a white-glove, end-to-end, cancer support service for patients and their families. We work with health plans across the country to provide 1-1 support to members facing a cancer diagnosis. All of our support is delivered through dedicated Oncology Certified Nurses, who work with members to catch cancer early, get them to fantastic experts for their care, and help them through the thousands of other problems patients and their families face. Join us to help serve cancer patients in their hour of need. The “Nurse Navigator” Role Our oncology nurse navigators are the front-line of CancerNavigator ’s patient service. Nurse Navigators support patients at all parts of their journey – newly diagnosed, in active treatment, and entering remission. With more specificity, oncology nurse navigators: Educate cancer patients (and their families) about their diagnosis, treatment options, and provide helpful information on any related questions and concerns the patient may have Work closely with the researchers on our team to deliver tailored information to patients, guiding them to the centers and doctors that would be a great option for the patient’s care Do everything possible to address any barriers to care (e.g. registering and scheduling appointments, coordinating with their health plan or their care team, transferring records, etc.) Provide longitudinal support to the patient throughout their journey – helping them solve any issues related to their cancer diagnosis and care – whether connecting patients to mental health support, finding resources to ease the financial burden, arranging transportation to appointments, or answering any questions that may arise The Requirements The main requirement of this role is oncology nursing experience and a passion for serving cancer patients. More specifically, we are looking for someone with the following experience and qualifications: Ability to work Eastern hours (8am-5pm EST) 3+ years of oncology nursing experience Mastery of common navigation and care coordination issues (registration, scheduling, clinical department navigation, insurance coordination, solving coverage issues, etc.) Mastery of basic computer tools (Gmail, Zoom, Word, PowerPoint, etc.) Preferred: Oncology Certified Nurse (OCN) Compensation and Benefits Starting Salary Range: $100-115k (based on skills and experience) Dental and Healthcare (80% employer paid), Vision Insurance (100% employer paid) Healthcare and Dependent Care FSA Group Life and AD&D Insurance (involuntary with the option to buy up coverage) Unlimited PTO Remote-first work; live where you want within the region All-company on-sites 2-3x per year (in Washington DC & Denver) Our Culture & Values, In Brief We’re building a company where what we do matters. The goal couldn’t be clearer – serve cancer patients. As the business grows, and the work becomes more complex, we need to become more, not less, committed to why we are doing this. Respect for our responsibility: We strive, as a team, to respect the gravity of the responsibility we bear to patients, always acting and producing in a way that is worthy of the trust they have placed in us.
